clue.text: Gather about a little page

parts.note: re is Latin-derived shorthand for about or concerning
P is the standard abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Someone collecting a small boy servant, or a short sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap a harvest is to gather in the crop.

clue.text: A way the old can show complaint

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way or road
ye is an old written form of the word 'the', as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: An elderly person finding a route to voice a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' here is a medical one: an ailment of the eyelid, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A small painful swelling on the eyelid is a minor ailment, a complaint in the medical sense.

clue.text: Bold fellow giving a girl a ring

parts.note: her is the pronoun used for a girl
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A brave man proposing to a young woman by offering her a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A courageous man admired for his daring is called a champion or brave fellow.

clue.text: Fresh start for a Frenchman having the regulation back-up

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, read upwards means the word is written backwards

parts.note: a law is a rule or regulation

explanation.surface: A Frenchman makes a new beginning with the rulebook as his support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-up' turns LAW into WAL, read from the bottom up in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A renewal is a revival or restart, a fresh beginning.

clue.text: Support it with promises to pay as opportune

parts.note: a prop is a support
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: Backing something with a few written debts at just the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Propitious means favourable, timely and well suited to the occasion.

clue.text: Bland nature of grub the head provided

parts.note: a gentle is an angler's word for a maggot, a grub used as bait
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Mild temperament made possible by food the boss supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food, but here it is a larva: GENTLE is an old angling term for a maggot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildness and softness of manner make up a bland, kindly disposition.

clue.text: Politicians ordering means test

indicators.note: ordering means putting these letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lawmakers demanding a check on people's income before benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' rearranges MEANS and TEST; a means test is a check on income before state help.
explanation.definitionFit: Statesmen are experienced political leaders.

clue.text: Not at all well done, which is exceptional

explanation.surface: A steak barely cooked, which is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that is underdone is described this way, and the same word means unusual or uncommon.

clue.text: Portray commercial traveller with grudge

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative who travels for a company
to resent something is to grudge it

explanation.surface: Describing a travelling salesman who bears a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict or show something is to portray it.

clue.text: Wonders if one he-man has been put straight by coppers

parts.note: P stands for pence, coppers being small copper coins

indicators.note: put straight means sorted out, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Marvels whether a muscleman has been reformed by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests the police but supplies P, pennies; 'has been put straight' rearranges ONE HEMAN into HENOMENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable things or marvels are called phenomena.

clue.text: Money in retirement? None whatsoever

indicators.note: retirement means going back, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: L stands for the pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A pensioner asks about savings and is told there are none.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns L and IN round to give the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil means nothing, zero.

clue.text: Whistle when a Greek character exercises

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A whistle blown while a Greek person works out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe is a simple wind instrument, and to pipe is to whistle shrilly.

clue.text: A great rock given to the monarch

parts.note: R stands for Rex or Regina, the king or queen

explanation.surface: A huge stone presented to the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a high rocky outcrop, typical of Dartmoor in south-west England.

clue.text: Impasse say about meal preparation

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to state is to say

indicators.note: preparation means making up, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A deadlock over how dinner should be made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preparation' rearranges MEAL into ALEM, and 'about' puts STATE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock where neither side can advance, from the chess position with no legal move.

clue.text: Give voice about a parent being overwhelming

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word is placed around the other

parts.note: to sing is to give voice
a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: Speaking up about a mother who is overbearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Smothering means stifling or overpowering, as with excessive affection.

clue.text: Some people stuff at home

indicators.note: stuff means packing inside, so the word at is filled with the other pieces

parts.note: a part is some of something
men are people

explanation.surface: A few people cram their belongings indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' looks like belongings, but it is a verb: PART and MEN are stuffed inside AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat or set of rooms where someone lives is their dwelling.

clue.text: The eccentric sees Latin as vital

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball thinks the Latin language is indispensable.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential means absolutely necessary.

clue.text: Lunches in an unpretentious cafe at slight expense

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words cafe at slight

explanation.surface: Someone has cheap midday meals in a simple diner.
explanation.definitionFit: To lunch is to have a meal, so lunches means consumes food.

clue.text: No harm's resulted from the use of such language

indicators.note: resulted means came out of a change, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: No damage came from speaking that tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resulted' rearranges NO HARMS; Romansh is a language of Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Romansh is a Romance tongue spoken in parts of Switzerland.

clue.text: Your worm is your only for diet."Hamlet

definitions.text: Your worm is your only for diet."Hamlet

parts.words: Your worm is your only for diet."Hamlet
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Hamlet: the missing word completes the line about worms ruling over the dead

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's line is 'Your worm is your only emperor for diet': the missing word is the gap in the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Hamlet's line names a supreme ruler, the worm reigning over what it eats.

clue.text: Time for a rise, Edward gave out

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is written backwards

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward announced it was time to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a rise' turns TIME upwards to EMIT in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give out or discharge.

clue.text: Note there are many on strike

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword shorthand for many
to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: A message saying lots of workers have walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A chit is a short written note or voucher.

clue.text: Names on it, quite improperly

indicators.note: improperly means wrongly arranged, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone has written names on something where they shouldn't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite improperly' rearranges NAMES ON IT; the whole clue also describes putting names forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose people for a post or award is to put their names forward.

clue.text: Set one's sights on really good figure

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the 1 read as the letter I
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a figure

explanation.surface: Targeting someone with a terrific body shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim is to point or direct at a target.

clue.text: Dull floor-covering

explanation.definitionFit: Matt, also spelt mat, describes a non-shiny finish, and a mat is a small rug for the floor.

clue.text: Rebel leader in charge, totally unrestrained

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the first letter of Rebel is used

explanation.surface: An insurgent chief in command acts without any limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like command, but it is a payment, FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Free means at liberty, without any restraint.

clue.text: At sea for the most part

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, out on the ocean (the main being the open sea); idiomatically, mostly or generally.

clue.text: A high-flier of sound merit

indicators.note: sound means as heard, so the word is spoken and respelt

parts.note: to earn something is to merit it

explanation.surface: A successful person who rightly deserves their success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flier' suggests a go-getter, but it is a bird: the sea eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: An erne is a sea eagle, a bird that soars high.

clue.text: Plays written for the new cast

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dramas written for a fresh company of actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts are performs, as an actor plays a role.

clue.text: Observe there's no cigarette-end to be seen here

parts.note: the end of the word cigarette is its final pair of letters

explanation.surface: A no-smoking notice where butts must not be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cigarette-end' looks like a stub, but supplies the end of the word cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to observe or notice it.

clue.text: Top-drawer nincompoop, this one!

parts.note: U means upper-class, the top drawer of society
a nit is a fool, a nincompoop

explanation.surface: An upper-class idiot singled out by the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, a whole number one.

clue.text: Appear lifeless before the public

parts.note: describes a dead dignitary displayed to mourners, not an actor playing dead

explanation.definitionFit: A dead dignitary displayed publicly before burial so mourners can pay respects.
